name: WIRES National Grants Program

funder.name: WIRES (NSW Wildlife Information, Rescue and Education Service)

summary: Competitive one-off grants across four tiers for Australian wildlife carers, rescue organisations, environmental NGOs, community groups and consortia, supporting wildlife rescue and rehabilitation, habitat restoration and native species recovery projects of 6 to 12 months.

amount.note: Top tier for consortia; environmental NGOs and community groups up to 10,000, carers up to 1,000, rescue organisations up to 5,000

eligibility.rule: Be a legal entity able to enter a legally binding agreement
Have operated in this capacity for at least 2 years
Have no overdue reports for previously funded grants
Have no current active grant with WIRES
Tier 1 or 2 applicants have held an appropriate permit for 2 years
Tier 3 or 4 applicants are Australian organisations with a current ABN

documents: Rehabilitation or vet licence, for Tier 1 or 2
Driver's licence or other authorised ID, if an individual
ABN and ACNC incorporation number, if applicable
Photos of existing setup, if applying for facility updates or repairs
Partner support letters with roles and resources, for Tier 3 or 4
Written consent of the site owner or manager, for Tier 3 or 4 sites the applicant does not own or manage

status.quote: Key dates for 2026 applications: Applications - Closed

applicant_types.quote: Tier 1: Individually Licensed Wildlife Rescuers and Carers (maximum $1,000) Tier 2: Licensed Wildlife Rescue and Rehabilitation Organisations (maximum $5,000) Tier 3: Environmental NGOs and Community Groups (maximum $10,000) Tier 4: Consortia/Multi-partner Collaborations (maximum $20,000)

geography.quote: Be located in and conduct activities within Australia

access.quote: eligible applicants are invited to apply

amount.quote: Tier 1: Individually Licensed Wildlife Rescuers and Carers (maximum $1,000) Tier 2: Licensed Wildlife Rescue and Rehabilitation Organisations (maximum $5,000) Tier 3: Environmental NGOs and Community Groups (maximum $10,000) Tier 4: Consortia/Multi-partner Collaborations (maximum $20,000)

pool.quote: A total funding pool of up to $200,000 is available across four tiers.

consortium_required.quote: Tier 1: Individually Licensed Wildlife Rescuers and Carers

effort.quote: To apply for a WIRES Grant, applicants must meet the eligibility criteria and accurately complete the application form for the appropriate funding tier and submit on time.
WIRES will conduct an eligibility check.
These collated applications will be assessed by the Assessment Panel.

eligibility.quote: Be a legal entity, able to enter into a legally binding agreement
have been operating in this capacity for a minimum of two years
Not have overdue progress or acquittal reports for previously funded grants
Not have a current active grant with WIRES
Grantees must have held an appropriate permit per the state they operate in for a minimum of two (2) years
Be registered as an Australian organisation with a current ABN and operate in Australia

after_award.quote: Reports due - Final for Tier 1 & 2 projects, Progress for Tier 3 & 4 projects May 2027 Final Report due and project completed - Tier 3 & 4 projects November 2027

documents.quote: Meet licensing requirements as outlined above for each state and provide a copy of their rehabilitation licence or vet licence

If an individual, provide a copy of their driver's licence or other authorised form of ID (e.g. passport) • If an organisation, provide their ABN and, if applicable, their ACNC incorporation number • Provide a reference (must not be the applicant, a member of the applicant's immediate family, or a member of the same group or collective)
Provide appropriate quotes for all budget lines of their proposal • If applying for updates to, or repairs/replacement of enclosures/facilities, provide photos of existing set up
Provide letters of support from partners including the roles/responsibilities the project partner will undertake, and the resources it will contribute (both cash and in-kind, if any)
Written consent is required from the property owner and/or property manager that allows for the implementation of the proposed project on each project site
